extra.message: runPatientRosterReport() builds a raw SQL string by concatenating the user-supplied filterValue into the WHERE clause ('%${filterValue}%') and the user-supplied sortField into ORDER BY, then executes it with prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(query). The report API (/api/reports) passes request query params filterValue and sortField straight through, allowing SQL injection (including ORDER BY injection since the ROSTER_SORT_COLUMNS allowlist is bypassed whenever sortField is not a known key).

extra.message: convertDocumentForRelease() interpolates the caller-supplied outputFormat (and sourcePath) into a shell command passed to child_process.exec(). /api/documents/convert reads outputFormat directly from the request body and forwards it, so an authenticated staff user can inject arbitrary shell metacharacters (e.g. "; rm -rf ...").

extra.message: renderDocumentFromTemplate() joins the attacker-controlled templateName onto TEMPLATE_DIR with path.join and readFileSync without confining the resolved path. /api/documents/[id]/letterhead passes the user-controlled 'letterheadTemplate' cookie value as templateName, enabling path traversal (e.g. ../../../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files. extra.message: archiveVisitPacket() writes a file to path.join(PACKET_DIR, `${packetLabel}.txt`) using the caller-supplied packetLabel without path.basename()/containment. POST /api/visit-summaries/[id]/packet accepts packetLabel from the JSON body, allowing an authenticated user to write files anywhere writable (e.g. ../../../public/shell.js) via path traversal. cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: saveLetterheadAsset() uses the raw multipart upload filename (file.name) in path.join(BRANDING_DIR, file.name) and writeFileSync() with no normalization, extension or MIME validation. POST /api/admin/branding accepts this file and BRANDING_DIR defaults to ./public/branding, so an admin/attacker controlling the filename can traverse out of the directory (e.g. ../../src/... or ../.env) and overwrite arbitrary files, including writing into the web-served public directory. extra.message: retrieveExternalLabReport() calls fetch(reportUrl) on a fully attacker-controlled URL with no scheme/host allowlist or private-IP filtering. POST /api/labs/inbound takes the URL from the 'lab-report-url' request header, so anyone able to reach the webhook (or who knows the shared LAB_FEED_SECRET) can make the server fetch internal services/cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/). extra.message: POST handler performs no requireAuth()/getCurrentUser() check and no role check. It reads the target clinician from the client-controlled 'x-kiosk-clinician-id' header and updates that clinician's specialty. Any unauthenticated caller can modify arbitrary clinician profiles. extra.message: resumeVendorSyncDestination() returns the caller-supplied rawDestination verbatim whenever it is non-empty. GET /api/appointments/sync passes the 'x-redirect-url' request header into it and then calls NextResponse.redirect(new URL(destination, request.url)), allowing an open redirect to any external site (e.g. https://evil.example.com). The sibling resumeDirectoryRefreshDestination() validates against an allowlist and is safe.

extra.message: resolveLabelAttachmentHeaders() builds the Content-Disposition header by directly interpolating displayTitle without stripping CR/LF. GET /api/prescriptions/[id]/label takes displayTitle from the 'document_title' query parameter and returns these headers, allowing HTTP response header injection via a title containing %0d%0a. The sibling resolvePacketAttachmentHeaders() strips [\r\n] and is safe.

extra.message: The download route sets Content-Disposition using document.originalName, which is the user-supplied multipart filename persisted at upload time and never sanitized. extra.message: traceMessageSearchActivity() writes the raw, unescaped searchQuery into a console.log line without stripping CR/LF/NUL. extra.message: issueLegacyLabFeedKey() generates a secret API key with Math.random(), a non-cryptographic PRNG with predictable state, making issued keys guessable/brute-forceable. The sibling issueClearinghouseFeedKey() uses crypto.randomBytes and is safe.

extra.message: reopenRefillDraft() decrypts attacker-controlled ciphertext using AES-256-CBC with no MAC/integrity protection, and catches decrypt failures to distinguish padding errors ('bad decrypt'/'padding') from other errors via a distinct message and HTTP 422 status (see /api/prescriptions/[id]/refill-draft). This creates a padding-oracle oracle over the shared DRAFT_KEY, allowing an attacker to decrypt/forge draft plaintext. The visit-summary variant correctly uses AES-256-GCM with an auth tag.

extra.message: loadApplicationConfig() passes arbitrary, unvalidated JSON from the request body straight into Object.assign(runtimeConfig, overrides). extra.message: POST takes a patient user id from the URL and calls startCounterAssistedPortalSession() to overwrite the caller's own session with that patient's session (session.userId = patient id), turning the caller into the patient. A front_desk or clinic_admin account can therefore take over any patient's account and access all of that patient's records. There is no per-request authorization binding (e.g. verification that the patient is checking in at the counter), which violates the spec's 'impersonation-free support workflow' requirement.

extra.message: startWaitingRoomCheckin() sets the 'sessionId' cookie with only { path: '/' }, omitting httpOnly, secure and sameSite attributes. The sibling startCounterAssistedPortalSession() uses hardened iron-session cookie handling and does not echo the id.
